avatar.summary: A round image for a user or account, showing initials or an icon instead when no picture is available.
avatar.useFor: Avatar stands in for a single user, team or account next to their name, in headers, comments and list rows. It handles the loading and broken-image case for you by swapping in initials or an icon.

neighbours.name: avatar-group
neighbours.guidance: Pick Avatar Group when several people share one spot and you want them overlapped with a +N count.

neighbours.name: badge
neighbours.guidance: Pick Badge for a text label about status or category; Avatar is only for identity.

rules: Compose `Avatar` with an `AvatarImage` and an `AvatarFallback`, so initials or an icon show while the image loads or if it fails.
Write a meaningful `alt` for the image. When the avatar shows only initials or an icon, add `role="img"` and an `aria-label` to `Avatar` itself.
Resize or reshape with classes such as `size-10` or a radius class, because there is no size or shape prop.
Use `status` for a presence dot and let it announce Online, Away, Busy or Offline; override the wording with `statusLabel` when translating.
Skip the accessible name when the person's name is already printed right beside the avatar, so it is not read twice.

avatar-group.summary: A facepile: several avatars overlapped in a row with an optional count of the people not shown.
avatar-group.useFor: Avatar Group shows that a set of people belongs to something, such as project members or reviewers, without listing each name. It handles the overlap, the separating ring and the overflow pill.

neighbours.name: avatar
neighbours.guidance: Pick a single Avatar when only one person is involved.

neighbours.name: resource-list
neighbours.guidance: Pick Resource List when every person needs their name and details visible on screen.

rules: Place `Avatar` children straight inside `AvatarGroup`, then end with an `AvatarGroupCount` for the hidden members.
Set `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`) on the group rather than on each avatar so the overlap and the count scale together.
Set `count` to the number of avatars left out, and pair it with screen-reader-only text naming what is counted, for example "more members".
Decide in your own code how many avatars to render; the group does not measure or trim its children.
On a custom surface, check that the ring colour matches the background, since it follows the kit surface it sits on.

badge.summary: A compact label for a status, category, plan or count, with semantic colour variants and fixed sizes.
badge.useFor: Badge tags a piece of content with a short word or number, such as Draft, Paid, New or an unread count. It also covers status-with-dot text, plan entitlements and a verified mark on an avatar.

neighbours.name: tag-group
neighbours.guidance: Pick Tag Group when the labels can be selected, removed or navigated with the keyboard.

neighbours.name: marker
neighbours.guidance: Pick Marker for a quiet status line inside a chat thread rather than a chip on a row.

rules: Choose `variant` by meaning (`success`, `warning`, `error`, `info`, `accent`, `secondary` and so on) and always keep a visible word beside the colour.
Use `profile="status"` for a coloured dot followed by the state in words, and `profile="count"` for a notification number that never truncates.
Give a count badge a contextual accessible name with hidden text, and hide decorative icons and dots from assistive technology.
Make a badge a link with `render`; otherwise it is a plain, non-interactive span and should not be used as a button.
Reserve `light` for the single announcement on a page, on an opaque variant.

file-type-icon.summary: A document-sheet icon that shows a file's type and extension, picked from its name.
file-type-icon.useFor: File Type Icon gives file lists, upload rows and attachment cards a quick visual cue for PDFs, spreadsheets, images, code and more. It reads only the file name, so it works before any upload has finished.

neighbours.name: attachment
neighbours.guidance: Pick Attachment when the file needs a full card with its name, upload state and actions; it can hold this icon as its media.

rules: Pass the file name as `name`, or set `extension` when the name has no suffix, such as a document title.
Always print the file name next to the icon, because the icon is `aria-hidden` and carries no text for assistive technology.
Pick a `size` of 16, 20, 24, 32 or 40; below 32 px the extension label is too small to read, so lean on the visible name.
Prefer a real thumbnail for images and videos when you have one, and keep this icon for rows without a preview.
Size outside the presets with a `className` that sets height and width in the 34:40 proportion.

card.summary: A surface that groups related content and actions, with header, panel, footer and framed-section parts.
card.useFor: Card is the default container for a block of an app screen, such as a form section, a summary, a list of invoices or a chart. It offers several surface treatments and a joined frame for titled sections that hold tables or stacked cards.

neighbours.name: settings-list
neighbours.guidance: Pick Settings List when every row is a labelled control; it already draws its own card and separators.

neighbours.name: data-list
neighbours.guidance: Put a Data List inside a Card when the content is label and value pairs for one record.

neighbours.name: glass
neighbours.guidance: Use the glass variant only when the card sits over a photo, video or colourful surface.

rules: Build with `CardHeader` (holding `CardMedia`, `CardTitle`, `CardDescription`, `CardAction`), then `CardPanel` and `CardFooter`.
Render the title as a heading with `render={<h2 />}` when it belongs in the page outline, because title parts are divs by default.
Do not wrap a card that contains buttons in another button or link; keep each control separate.
Pick the surface with `variant` (`raised`, `subtle`, `header`, `inset`, `elevated`, `message`, `error`, `glass`) and the padding with `density` or the `--sp-rw-card-inset` tokens.
Use `CardFrame` with `CardFrameBleed` to run a table edge to edge so its columns line up with the frame header.

data-list.summary: Label and value rows that describe one record, laid out side by side or stacked.
data-list.useFor: Data List shows the properties of a single thing, such as an account, an invoice or a deployment, as a description list. It suits detail panels, summary cards and side drawers.

neighbours.name: table
neighbours.guidance: Pick Table when people compare, sort or select many records instead of reading one.

neighbours.name: settings-list
neighbours.guidance: Pick Settings List when each row holds a control that changes a value.

neighbours.name: native-table
neighbours.guidance: Pick Native Table when the data has several columns per row rather than one label and one value.

rules: Compose `DataList` with one `DataListItem` per property, each holding a `DataListLabel` and a `DataListValue` so labels and values pair up for screen readers.
Switch to `orientation="vertical"` in narrow columns or for long values.
Set `--data-list-label-width` when several lists stack and their value columns should line up.
Turn on `dividers` to separate rows with hairlines; inline parts such as Badge, Code or a link can sit in a value.
Keep it read-only and stateless; it renders on the server and has no editing behaviour.

tag-group.summary: A keyboard-navigable set of tags that can be selected or removed, with animated adds and removals.
tag-group.useFor: Tag Group shows a collection of short labels that people interact with, such as applied filters, project labels or chosen recipients. It handles arrow-key focus, removal by keyboard and focus recovery after a tag leaves.

neighbours.name: badge
neighbours.guidance: Pick Badge for a static label that nobody selects or removes.

neighbours.name: filter-bar
neighbours.guidance: Inside a Filter Bar, put the removable tags in its active-filters row.

rules: Make a tag selectable with `selected` plus `onSelectedChange`, or with `defaultSelected` for tag-owned state.
Providing `onRemove` gives each tag a remove button and keyboard deletion; drop the tag from your state in the handler and label the button with `removeLabel`.
Use stable React keys, never the index, or the wrong tag animates out.
Render `Tag` elements directly inside `TagGroup` (fragments are fine) and do not wrap each tag in your own component.
Set `size` once on the group so every tag matches.

table.summary: An interactive data grid with keyboard navigation, sortable columns, row selection and row actions.
table.useFor: Table is for rows people work with: sorting, selecting, opening or running a command on a record. It acts as one tab stop with arrow-key movement, and leaves data loading, paging and sorting logic to your app.

neighbours.name: native-table
neighbours.guidance: Pick Native Table for read-only content or cells full of inputs that need their own tab stops.

neighbours.name: resource-list
neighbours.guidance: Pick Resource List for a one-column list of entities with a status marker and a little metadata.

neighbours.name: data-list
neighbours.guidance: Pick Data List to show the fields of a single record.

rules: Put `TableHead` cells directly in `TableHeader`, mark the identifying column with `isRowHeader`, and give rich rows a plain `textValue`.
Give the table a name with `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or a direct `TableCaption`.
For sorting, set `allowsSorting`, handle `onSortChange`, update `sortDescriptor` and reorder the data yourself.
For bulk selection use `selectionMode="multiple"` with `selectionTrigger="checkbox"` and `TableSelectionCheckbox`, and handle a `Selection` that can be the string "all".
Show empty results with `TableBody renderEmptyState`, and set `aria-busy` on the surrounding region while loading since there is no loading prop.
Let wide tables scroll inside their container instead of squeezing columns.

native-table.summary: A plain HTML table in the same look as Table, for reports and cells whose controls keep their own tab stops.
native-table.useFor: Native Table renders real table elements for content people read, such as reports, price lists, estimates and markdown tables. Inputs and buttons inside cells behave normally and can belong to a surrounding form.

neighbours.name: table
neighbours.guidance: Pick Table when rows are sorted, selected or activated with arrow-key navigation.

neighbours.name: data-list
neighbours.guidance: Pick Data List for a single record's label and value pairs.

neighbours.name: typeset
neighbours.guidance: Typeset already maps markdown tables onto Native Table, so do not wire it by hand there.

rules: Name the table with `aria-label` or a `NativeTableCaption` placed first inside `NativeTable`.
The first cell that identifies a row should be a `NativeTableHead` carrying `scope="row"`.
Use `tone` on `NativeTableRow` for `section`, `total` or `muted` rows, and turn off hover on section rows with `hoverable={false}`.
Set `align="end"` on number columns so digits line up, and on their headings too.
Set `minWidth` when columns need more room than a phone gives, so the table scrolls inside its container.
Do sorting, filtering, paging and totals in your app; the table holds no state.

resource-list.summary: A list of entities with a status indicator, title, description and meta slot, optionally clickable as links.
resource-list.useFor: Resource List shows projects, tasks, deployments or similar items as compact rows with a coloured marker and trailing metadata. It works as navigation when rows are links and animates rows as they are added or removed.

neighbours.name: table
neighbours.guidance: Pick Table when people compare several columns or need sorting and multi-select.

neighbours.name: data-list
neighbours.guidance: Pick Data List for the fields of one record rather than many records.

neighbours.name: timeline
neighbours.guidance: Pick Timeline when the rows are events in time order joined by a connector.

rules: Set `interactive` on `ResourceListItem` and render an anchor to make rows links; mark the current one with `active`.
Give every `ResourceListIndicator` a `label` (and an `icon` if useful) so status is not carried by colour alone.
Render rows as direct children with stable keys so add, remove and reorder animations track the right row.
Use `variant` (`soft` or `divided`), `density` and `flush` to match the surrounding card or filter bar.
Reach for List Box instead when you need managed keyboard selection; `selected` here only changes appearance on static and link rows.

filter-bar.summary: A layout strip above a list or table for view tabs, search, filter menus, actions and applied-filter tags.
filter-bar.useFor: Filter Bar arranges the controls that narrow a collection, from a plain search field to view tabs that open into a search. It only lays things out: the query, the filter values and the filtering itself stay in your app.

neighbours.name: tag-group
neighbours.guidance: Use a Tag Group inside `FilterBarActiveFilters` to show the filters currently applied.

neighbours.name: table
neighbours.guidance: Place the Filter Bar above a Table or Resource List; results states belong to the collection, not the bar.

rules: Group parts with `FilterBarControls`, `FilterBarSearch`, `FilterBarFilters`, `FilterBarActiveFilters` and `FilterBarActions` inside `FilterBar`.
When a search sits alongside a handful of views, put `TabsTab` items inside `FilterBarTabs`. Filter your rows from `query`, and give the tab list a label describing the views it changes.
Set `open` on `FilterBarActiveFilters` to whether any filter applies, so the row collapses smoothly when the last one goes.
Keep loading, error and empty states with the results, and never reset a search field that has focus.
Announce meaningful result changes politely rather than on every keystroke.

settings-list.summary: A titled card of settings rows, each pairing a label and help text with a control you supply.
settings-list.useFor: Settings List builds preference and account pages where each row is one setting with a switch, select, input or action button. It wires the labels and descriptions to the control and handles the responsive stacking.

neighbours.name: data-list
neighbours.guidance: Pick Data List when the rows only show values and nothing is editable.

neighbours.name: card
neighbours.guidance: Pick a plain Card when the content is not a set of individual settings.

rules: Give `SettingsList` a `title` (set `titleLevel` to fit the page outline) and give each `SettingsListItem` a `title`.
Render the control in the `control` render prop and spread every prop it receives so the label and description stay linked.
Buttons like Change or Manage should get `aria-describedby` and nothing more, so their visible text remains the accessible name.
Keep values, saving and validation in your app state; the list only draws the layout.
Use `layout="inline"` for small controls like switches and leave wide text controls on the default `responsive` layout.

stepper.summary: An ordered list of steps showing which are done, current, open or blocked, with optional clickable steps.
stepper.useFor: Stepper shows progress through a sequence such as onboarding or setup, and can reveal the content of the step that is open. It is a display and navigation aid; your app decides when a step is complete.

neighbours.name: timeline
neighbours.guidance: Pick Timeline for past events in date order rather than steps someone moves through.

neighbours.name: progress
neighbours.guidance: Pick Progress when only a percentage matters and the steps have no names.

rules: Use `StepperItem` for read-only steps and `StepperButtonItem` for every step people can open, without mixing the two for the same step.
Set `status` (`done`, `current`, `open`, `blocked`) for progress and `active` on a button item for which step is open; they are independent.
Pass children to show content under a step; it sits outside the button, so it can hold fields and links.
Keep or translate `statusLabel`, because done and blocked are shown only as icons visually.
Collapsed step content turns inert, so shift focus forward yourself once a step closes.

timeline.summary: A vertical list of events in time order with coloured or icon markers and an optional now line.
timeline.useFor: Timeline presents activity feeds, deploy histories, audit logs and a day's appointments. Events animate in and out as the list changes, and a now marker can sit between past and upcoming items.

neighbours.name: stepper
neighbours.guidance: Pick Stepper when the items are steps a person works through, not events that happened.

neighbours.name: resource-list
neighbours.guidance: Pick Resource List when order in time is not the point and each row is an entity.

rules: Render each `TimelineItem` directly inside `Timeline`, not inside a fragment, with `TimelineTitle` and `TimelineDescription`.
Set `tone` for status colour and keep the status in text as well.
Pass an icon as `marker`, and add `markerLabel` only when the marker says something the text does not.
Use `TimelineNow` between events to mark the present, passing `label` in the page language.
Wrap timestamps in `time` elements with a machine-readable `dateTime`, and supply events already sorted.

bar-chart.summary: Columns or horizontal bars that compare values across categories, grouped or stacked, with keyboard tooltips.
bar-chart.useFor: Bar Chart compares a handful to a few dozen categories, such as months, plans or regions, and handles negative values and rankings. It suits dashboard cards where people read totals side by side.

neighbours.name: line-chart
neighbours.guidance: Pick Line Chart for a trend over many dates where the shape matters more than each bar.

neighbours.name: bar-list
neighbours.guidance: Pick Bar List for a short ranked list of labels with values and no axis.

neighbours.name: pie-chart
neighbours.guidance: Pick Pie Chart only for a few shares of one total.

rules: Pass `data`, the `x` key, the `series` list and a required `label` that names the chart.
Use `stacked` for parts of a total and `orientation="horizontal"` for rankings with long category names.
Format numbers with `formatValue` and categories with `formatX`, and set `locale` to match the page.
Use `palette="categorical"` for unrelated series and `negativeColor` on a series for values below zero.
Keep category keys stable between data sets so bars glide instead of jumping, and translate the screen-reader words with `labels`.
Do not expect click or selection events; the chart is a read-only focus stop.

line-chart.summary: Lines on a shared axis that show how one or more measures rise and fall over time or ordered steps.
line-chart.useFor: Line Chart shows trends such as active users per month or orders per hour, with up to about five series. It supports date axes, several curve styles and a crosshair tooltip that works by keyboard.

neighbours.name: area-chart
neighbours.guidance: Pick Area Chart when the size of the measure or how parts stack into a total matters.

neighbours.name: bar-chart
neighbours.guidance: Pick Bar Chart when the categories have no natural order.

neighbours.name: sparkline
neighbours.guidance: Pick Sparkline for a tiny axis-free trend beside a number.

rules: Pass `data`, the `x` key, `series` and a required `label`.
Use `Date` objects at midnight UTC for a time axis; text x values are treated as categories.
Keep `curve="monotone"` unless you have a reason, since it never overshoots the data; use `step` for values that jump.
Write values with `formatValue` and set `locale`; missing values break the line rather than dropping to zero.
Use `height="fill"` with `minHeight` to fill a card's remaining height.

area-chart.summary: Filled areas over time, overlaid or stacked, so the size of a measure and its parts read at a glance.
area-chart.useFor: Area Chart shows volume over time, such as page views, and when stacked shows how sources add up to a total. It shares the line chart's axes, curves and keyboard tooltip.

neighbours.name: line-chart
neighbours.guidance: Pick Line Chart when multiple series do not add up to a total; overlapping fills would obscure one another.

neighbours.name: bar-chart
neighbours.guidance: Pick Bar Chart for a few discrete periods or unordered categories.

neighbours.name: sparkline
neighbours.guidance: Pick Sparkline with the area variant for a small inline trend.

rules: Pass `data`, the `x` key, `series` and a required `label`.
Use `stacked` when series are parts of one total; the tooltip still shows each series' own value.
Choose `fill="gradient"` or `fill="solid"`; both keep a line along the top.
Prefer the default `monotone` curve for data that rests on zero so the fill never dips below it.
Format values with `formatValue` and translate the screen-reader text with `labels`.

pie-chart.summary: A donut or pie that shows how one total splits into a few shares, with an optional figure in the hole.
pie-chart.useFor: Pie Chart suits storage usage, plan mix or traffic split, where there are only a few parts of one whole. The donut can show a total in its centre and an unfilled remainder share.

neighbours.name: bar-chart
neighbours.guidance: Pick Bar Chart when there are more than five or six shares or values need precise comparison.

neighbours.name: bar-list
neighbours.guidance: Pick Bar List for a ranked breakdown that reads better as rows.

rules: Pass `data` items with a stable `id`, a `label` and a `value`, plus a required chart `label`.
Mark the unused remainder with `empty` so it takes the neutral colour.
Show a total with `centerValue` and `centerLabel` (format with `centerFormat`), or pass short custom `center` content.
Sort the data on purpose: slices are drawn in array order, starting at the top and going clockwise.
Leave room around the chart when `popOut` is on, because the active share steps up to 10 px outside its box.

bar-list.summary: A ranked list of labels with a bar behind each, sized against the largest value.
bar-list.useFor: Bar List shows top pages, top countries or traffic sources as rows you can compare at a glance. It renders fully on the server and glides to new values when the period changes.

neighbours.name: bar-chart
neighbours.guidance: Pick Bar Chart if any value may fall below zero or readers need an axis to compare against.

neighbours.name: table
neighbours.guidance: Pick Table when rows need several values or must be clickable.

neighbours.name: resource-list
neighbours.guidance: Pick Resource List when a row should open or select something.

rules: Pass `data` sorted in the order you want ranked, each item with a unique `id`, a `label` and a `value`, and name the list with `label`.
Add a `heading` with `label` and `value` to name the two columns.
Format values with `formatValue` or set `locale`; use `description` for a quieter second line such as a path.
Keep a custom `color` light, because labels are written on top of the bars.
Rows are display-only: they do not respond to clicks, hover or focus, so do not wire actions to them.

sparkline.summary: A tiny axis-free chart that shows the shape of a trend next to the number it belongs to.
sparkline.useFor: Sparkline sits beside a KPI, inside a table cell or in a line of text to show whether a measure is rising or falling. It has no tooltip or axes and draws in the surrounding text colour.

neighbours.name: line-chart
neighbours.guidance: Pick Line Chart when readers need exact values, dates or a shared axis.

neighbours.name: area-chart
neighbours.guidance: Pick Area Chart for a full-size filled trend with a tooltip.

rules: Pass `data` as an array of numbers, or an array of arrays for several series on one scale.
Write a `label` that says what is shown and over which period, and print the actual figure beside it.
Set the colour from the parent text colour (for example a success or destructive class) or with `color`.
Give it a width class such as `w-24` and a pixel `height` in tight spots.
Set `includeZero={false}` when small changes on a large value would otherwise look flat.

message-scroller.summary: The scroll region of a chat thread: opens at the latest message, follows streaming replies and offers a jump back.
message-scroller.useFor: Message Scroller holds the turns of a chat or AI conversation, keeps a new turn in view, follows a reply as it streams and keeps position when older messages load above. It also acts as a log so screen readers hear new rows.

neighbours.name: message
neighbours.guidance: Use Message inside each row to lay out a single turn.

neighbours.name: marker
neighbours.guidance: Use Marker rows between turns for dates, notes and a thinking status.

neighbours.name: prompt-input
neighbours.guidance: Place Prompt Input below the scroller as the composer.

rules: Make every row a `MessageScrollerItem` directly inside `MessageScrollerContent`, with a stable `messageId` that also serves as the React key.
Mark the first row of each turn with `scrollAnchor`; that is normally the user's own message.
Turn on `autoScroll` to follow a growing reply, and set `busy` on `MessageScrollerContent` while a reply is pending.
Add `MessageScrollerButton` for the jump-to-latest control and use `useMessageScroller()` for custom jumps.
Load long histories in pages above the first row; rows are not virtualised.

message.summary: The layout of one chat turn: content, footer actions and, between people, an avatar and header.
message.useFor: Message arranges a single turn in a conversation, placing bubbles, attachments, traces and actions in the right order and on the right side. It draws no surface itself and keeps no state.

neighbours.name: bubble
neighbours.guidance: Use Bubble inside a Message for the text surface itself.

neighbours.name: marker
neighbours.guidance: Pick Marker for a line that is not a turn, such as a date or system note.

neighbours.name: message-scroller
neighbours.guidance: Wrap many Messages in a Message Scroller for the thread's scrolling and announcements.

rules: Compose `Message` with `MessageContent`, and add `MessageHeader`, `MessageFooter` and `MessageAvatar` as needed.
Set `align="end"` for the writer's own turns and give the Bubbles inside the same `align`.
Back-to-back messages from the same sender belong in one `MessageGroup`; give the earlier ones an empty `MessageAvatar` to keep them aligned.
Each footer icon action needs an `aria-label`. A footer with nothing in it takes up no space, so it is safe to render before any actions arrive.
Show a failed reply as a destructive Bubble with a Try again button and no rating actions.

bubble.summary: The surface for a chat message's text, with variants for sender, assistant replies and errors.
bubble.useFor: Bubble draws the coloured or bordered shape around message text and sizes it to its content. A ghost variant drops the surface for assistant answers and rich content like lists and code.

neighbours.name: message
neighbours.guidance: Pick Message to arrange the turn around the bubble, with avatar and actions.

neighbours.name: card
neighbours.guidance: Pick Card for content blocks outside a conversation.

rules: Compose `Bubble` with a `BubbleContent` that holds the text.
Choose `variant` by sender: `muted` for the person in an AI chat, `ghost` for assistant answers, `default` or `tinted` for your own messages between people, `destructive` for failures.
Set `align` to match the surrounding Message.
Put links or buttons inside the bubble or in the Message footer, since the bubble itself is not interactive.
Never let the colour alone say what happened; write it in the text.

marker.summary: A low-key line between chat messages for things like status updates, system notes or date dividers.
marker.useFor: Marker covers the in-between lines of a conversation: a thinking indicator, a stopped-reply note, a model change or a Today separator. It sits as its own row between turns or inside a turn's content.

neighbours.name: message
neighbours.guidance: Pick Message for anything a participant actually said.

neighbours.name: trace
neighbours.guidance: Pick Trace for the list of steps an agent took, with expandable details.

neighbours.name: badge
neighbours.guidance: Pick Badge for a chip on a row rather than a full-width thread line.

rules: Compose `Marker` with an optional `MarkerIcon` and a `MarkerContent`.
Set `role="status"` on lines that change, such as a live Thinking status, so they are announced.
Use `variant="separator"` for dates and breaks, and `variant="border"` for a note that heads the thread.
Put a Spinner in `MarkerIcon` for a reply in progress and hide decorative icons from assistive tech (the part does this).
Keep important wording in the text because the marker colour is deliberately muted.

trace.summary: One-line rows for an AI agent's reasoning, tool calls and sources that expand into their details.
trace.useFor: Trace shows what an agent did before it answered: thinking time, searches, tool results, failures and the sources it used. Each row can open into output such as a code block, and summaries can nest further steps.

neighbours.name: marker
neighbours.guidance: Pick Marker for a single status line or note with no details to expand.

neighbours.name: accordion
neighbours.guidance: Pick Accordion for general expandable sections outside an agent transcript.

rules: Build each row from a `TraceLine` with `TraceIcon`, `TraceTitle` and `TraceDescription`, wrapped in a `TraceCollapsibleTrigger` or a `TraceLink` to make it act.
Set `status` to `running`, `error` or `pending`; leave it off for finished work.
Put the state in the title words (present tense while running, past tense when done) since screen readers do not hear colour or shimmer.
Ask for tool approval in an Alert after the Trace, not as a row.
Pass `keepMounted` to `TraceCollapsibleContent` when a summary nests another Trace whose open state should survive.

attachment.summary: A card for a file or image attached to a message or draft, with upload states and actions.
attachment.useFor: Attachment shows files in a chat composer, in a sent message or in an upload row, including progress, failures and retry. Cards can sit in a horizontally scrolling group and open a preview.

neighbours.name: file-type-icon
neighbours.guidance: Use File Type Icon on its own for a simple list row without upload state or actions.

neighbours.name: prompt-input
neighbours.guidance: Inside Prompt Input, put small attachment cards in `PromptInputAttachments`.

rules: Set `state` (`idle`, `uploading`, `processing`, `error`, `done`) from your upload code, and say the state in `AttachmentDescription` too.
Give every `AttachmentAction` and `AttachmentTrigger` an `aria-label` that includes the file name.
Use `orientation="vertical"` with `AttachmentMedia variant="image"` for image thumbnails and `size="sm"` inside fields.
Wrap rows in `AttachmentGroup` with a `label` and stable keys, and move focus elsewhere before removing a card.
Remember the card uploads nothing; your app starts, retries and cancels uploads.

prompt-input.summary: Chat input that submits on Enter, expands as the draft gets longer, and swaps Send for Stop during a response.
prompt-input.useFor: Prompt Input is the message field at the bottom of a chat or AI assistant, with room for attachments, an attach button and model or effort pickers. It speaks the AI SDK's status words, so it plugs into `useChat` directly.

neighbours.name: textarea
neighbours.guidance: Pick Textarea for an ordinary multi-line form field that is submitted with the rest of a form.

neighbours.name: attachment
neighbours.guidance: Use Attachment cards inside it for files in the draft.

neighbours.name: message-scroller
neighbours.guidance: Pair it with Message Scroller above for the thread.

rules: Handle `onSubmit`, which receives the trimmed text, then add the message to your thread yourself.
Pass `status` (`ready`, `submitted`, `streaming`, `error`) and `onStop` so Send becomes Stop while a reply runs.
Compose `PromptInputTextarea`, `PromptInputToolbar` with `PromptInputToolbarGroup`, `PromptInputAttachButton` and `PromptInputSubmit`.
Use `submitOnEnter="desktop"` when phone users should get new lines from Enter.
Set `allowEmpty` only while the draft holds a file that is ready to send, and translate the built-in names through `labels`.
Placeholder text does not count as a label, so the field still needs an accessible name.

typeset.summary: Applies the kit's typography to rendered markdown, like chat replies or docs, by mapping elements to components.
typeset.useFor: Typeset gives markdown output from react-markdown or Streamdown consistent headings, lists, code blocks, quotes and tables. It copes with streaming answers that grow block by block.

neighbours.name: native-table
neighbours.guidance: Typeset renders markdown tables with Native Table already; use Native Table directly only for hand-built tables.

neighbours.name: bubble
neighbours.guidance: Put Typeset inside a ghost Bubble for an assistant answer.

rules: Pass `typesetComponents` to your renderer's `components` prop and place the output inside `Typeset`.
Choose `density="chat"` for answers in a thread and `density="document"` for longer standalone reading.
With Streamdown, give its wrapper `className="contents space-y-0"` and pass `streaming` to `TypesetCodeBlock` while a fence is still open.
Add `remark-gfm` to react-markdown if answers contain tables.
Use Typeset only for written prose, not for interface labels in forms or cards.

animated-buttons.summary: Buttons that animate on hover with sweeping or pass-through fills, a moving arrow, actions that expand, and entrance effects.
animated-buttons.useFor: Animated Buttons add tactile motion to marketing calls to action, carousel arrows, learn-more links and a log out control. They keep normal Button behaviour and finish instantly under reduced motion.

neighbours.name: button
neighbours.guidance: Pick plain Button for everyday app actions where motion would distract.

neighbours.name: icon-morphs
neighbours.guidance: Pick Icon Morphs for a menu toggle whose bars turn into a close icon.

rules: Use `FillSweepButton` with `sweep` (`reverse` or `through`), `arrow` (`bare` or `tile`) and `arrowDirection` for the hover effects.
Give arrow-only buttons an `aria-label`, since they have no visible text.
Use `ExpandingArrowButton` for a link-style action and `ExpandingLogoutButton` for log out, where `label` doubles as the accessible name.
Treat `entrance` (`grow`, `widen`, `fade`) as a one-time mount effect; remount to replay it.
Make sure each action is clear without the motion, because disabled, loading and reduced-motion states do not animate.

icon-morphs.summary: A menu button whose bars morph into an X while its navigation panel is open.
icon-morphs.useFor: Icon Morphs provides the hamburger toggle for mobile and compact navigation. It owns its expanded state attribute and label, and pairs well with a Collapsible panel.

neighbours.name: toggle
neighbours.guidance: Pick Toggle for an on/off control that does not open navigation.

neighbours.name: theme-toggles
neighbours.guidance: Pick Theme Toggles for a light and dark switch.

rules: Use `MenuIconMorph` with `open` and `onOpenChange`, or `defaultOpen` for local state.
Point `aria-controls` at the navigation element it shows and hides.
Keep the built-in open and close labels or pass your own `aria-label`.
Feed the same `open` value to a Collapsible that holds the navigation so both move together.
Use `onClick` with `preventDefault()` only when you must cancel the toggle.

theme-toggles.summary: Animated sun and moon toggles that switch an app between light and dark mode.
theme-toggles.useFor: Theme Toggles give a header or settings row a single control for dark mode with a sun-to-moon animation. They report state only; your theme provider applies the change.

neighbours.name: toggle-group
neighbours.guidance: Pick Toggle Group when people choose among light, dark and system.

neighbours.name: switch
neighbours.guidance: Pick Switch for a labelled dark mode setting inside a settings form.

rules: Drive `SunMoonMorphToggle` or `LayeredThemeToggle` so that `pressed` is true in dark mode, and change the theme from `onPressedChange`.
Drive `pressed` from your resolved theme so the icon and the app never disagree, including portalled overlays.
Keep the accessible name constant (default Dark mode) and let `aria-pressed` report the state.
Size it with `size` or let it follow the provider.

glass.summary: Frosted, see-through takes on Card, Button, Menu, Context Menu, Popover and Tooltip, meant to sit on top of photos.
glass.useFor: Glass lets controls and cards float over photos, video, maps or colourful surfaces while staying legible. It is a `variant` on existing components rather than a component of its own.

neighbours.name: card
neighbours.guidance: Keep the default Card surface on plain pages, where glass shows almost nothing.

neighbours.name: popover
neighbours.guidance: Set the glass tone attributes on the popup itself, since popovers render outside their trigger.

rules: Set `variant="glass"` on Button, Tooltip, Popover, Menu, Context Menu, Card or `DropdownMenuContent`.
Use it only with a picture or colour behind it; on a flat background keep the default surface.
Switch to a lighter panel with `data-glass-tone="light"` or dark text with `data-glass-ink="dark"`, on the component or a wrapper.
Check text contrast against your real imagery and keep long text on a solid surface.
